This was one of the first games I bought on Steam, and I stand by my decision to buy it after all these years. It is a game that puts an unique spin on the RPG item shop staple, by forcing you to take a crash course in profit-making, stock management, and haggling. Hell, calling this Baby's First Management wouldn't be far off if the game wasn't so unforgivable on those that don't cater to their clients (Then again, it's not like starting from the beginning was a brutal punishment when you keep your things, but still).
Fans of dungeon crawling, on the other hand, won't be dissapointed as the adventuring feels very well done, and, more importantly, each of your mercenary pals not only plays differently, they really feel differently, right down to movement and battle mechanics. This might not seem strange in a game tailored around the theme, but in a game focused on store management this comes as a pleasant surprise.
Also, the ammount of content in this game is absurd: The story itself isn't exactly long, and as you struggle against the loan deadlines you may come to loathe the moment when no other shoppers try to buy something it may feel short, but trying to get all the true adventurer cards, trying to fill out your in-game glossary, and really, just trying to get the true end itself will feel like you're playing one of those JRPGs that have no end in sight after a hundred hours.
If the economics, the dungeon crawling and the collecting still haven't sold you into it, maybe you'll give it a shot for the sheer hillarity and referencing in this game. And remember, the demo is there to help you make a more informed decision than what the shopkeeper tells you, so give it a shot before buying. Finally, it's not like you can't haggle the price down, if you decide to buy it eventually, after all, that's what steam sales are for. Capitalism, ho!

I've never written a Steam review before, but really wanted to sing the praises of this game.
I'm someone who loves to drive in real life, and who also comes from and lives in California. I'm a fan of EuroTruck Simulator 2 (and I also lived in the UK for 5 years), but felt a lot of the scenery and layout was very repetitive and would often uninstall after only a few play sessions, although I'd reinstall it once in awhile. Solid game tho, and the business tycoon style aspect was fun.
In American Truck Simulator you really have the same game however I strongly feel they've done a fantastic job of skinning the game in such a way that really gives the feeling and spirit of the American Southwest very well. I know and have driven many times around the places in this game and while it's not 100% perfect or to scale, there's a ton of subtleties that this game gives to very much put you in something a lot like real life.
The windmills off Highway 111 (down in what is effectly the Coachella Valley, where Palm Springs is), the tree barriers found off Highway 99 that runs along the eastern side of the San Juaqin Valley (which is very different to the feel of the 5 Freeway which runs down the west side of that huge valley), the way the roads and buildings change while you drive over the Sierra Nevada pass (past Truckee) and into Nevada itself. The way the roads work around Las Vegas. All of these examples and hundreds more really give you a strong sense of what it is to drive around this part of the world, with all of the other successful elements from EuroTruck Simulator 2, including the ability to customize your music, and even just use preexisting Internet Radio streams which are all highly appropriate, to managing your own company of trucks and drivers over time.
Getting better in the game requires coming to learn what different areas of the map will throw at you to slow you down or trip you up, eg parts of a freeway being subject to harsh speed limits (and getting a huge speed fine if you miss it) or understanding that making a left onto a freeway from a country lane could take you an extra half an hour, or knowing when sharp grades are better driven around than attempted head on, all of these things are at play and create a real sense of accomplishment over time as you begin to master the routes.
This is a very fun game that's just as good as its predecessor but I think a much more realistic and engaging experience than Euro 2. The only complaint I have is some minor AI issues that can occur around some intersections and a funny thing where some intersections have both stop lights and stop signs too which seem to confuse the AI (and also isn't how America traffic works either). It's a pretty minor problem though that may even disappear someday.
Defininte recommend for anyone who liked the predecessors.

*Read to the bottom for an understanding of why I'm recommending*
The game has a long way to go to be playable. While the features currently in the game are on their way to being acceptable, there seems to be a lot missing. The user interface needs some help and can make the game physcially difficult to play. The concept is refreshing and fun though and I have hope for this game if the developers continue. I go into further detail below:
Features Issues:
- Flight is difficult to manage, as you have to click a  move key, then click the mouse  on the ground. However, that doesn't always register in certain "dead zones" on the landscape.
- Lacking tutorials. The tutorials at the beginning of the game are hard to read (more on that later) and the names don't always match the interface (such as "job" being "contract") .
- Overall lacking explanation. Why are certain engines called "demons"? At least I think they're engines because I can't tell what else they do because of a lack of information on the world as a whole. Additionally, the strekoleks are airplanes. It took me about half an hour to discover that on accident, having previously read the name several times with no idea what it was.
Interface Issues:
- The text is tiny
- The screen feels pushed towards the center and poorly optimized for larger screens
- Tutorial windows need to be close to the view of the user, though they are scaled with the objects in game. They should appear almost like a menu, overlaying everything else and much larger.
Pros:
- Great concept
- Airship idea is great
- RPG/Strategy mix is a nice touch
- Base-building is nice to see in a game (rare)
- The idea of commanding a fleet is cool
Bottom Line:
This game needs polish and refinement. It needs more features, a better map and better interface with widescreen support. Also, the controls need to be reconsidered. Otherwise, it stands a chance of being a wonderfully exciting game. I  am recommending this because of its concept and potential. This concept is rare and we really need more "thinking" games like this that actually let us experience a world and econimic/strategic features without being confined to the traditional "Find resources, build soldiers, throw soldiers at enemy" scheme.

I hate post-apocalyptic games. I hated Fallout, played it for 1 hours before getting bored and requesting for a refund. First question that might come to your head; "Do I have to play Metro 2033 to understand this game?" No. You don't have to play Metro 2033, I didn't play it and I still could understand the story perfectly fine(though I will definitely play 2033) This game has it's intense moments, running away from mutants because you will run out of ammo if you try and fight them, stepping on a swamp and then wiping your air mask's eye protector, your air mask also can be broken during fights and you'll need to switch to a fresh air mask every once in a while. Gameplay was freaking awesome, escaping from disgusting beasts while trying to find air filters in order not to suffocate, damn was it intense. There are several ways to play the game which is great to say the least, stealth, sneaking by, killing everyone on the way. I did stealth when I felt like it, killed everyone on the way when I felt like it, could never sneak by though. The atmosphere is seriously amazing as well, it immerses you into the Metro universe. This game is probably post apocalyptic games done right.

Bullet point reviews, ho~!
Pros
- A fun hybrid of shop management and action RPG questing
- The translation is surprisingly entertaining and appropriately silly
- Taking heroes on quests only to sell the best stuff they find back to them at 300% markup is pretty great
- A surprisingly long RPG quest campaign with multiple adventurers, dungeons, and secrets to find
- I sold month-old egg on toast for a thousand bucks. Take that, economy!
Cons
- Selling items becomes a bit formulaic; most new shop-related stuff (custom orders, etc.) show up early and don't introduce anything new later on
- Dungeons can be a grind for XP and items, and the limited bag space (which is upgradable) is a chore
- Music is fun at first, intolerable in large quantities
- Recette's Japanese exclamations when she does anything are incredibly obnoxious
- I pressed "Esc --> Skip Scene" more in this game than maybe any to date
- Made me feel like the Wal-Mart of the fantasy world when I would only sell severely marked up junk to housewives just before the market crashed and everybody was poor
- I hate little girls
Conclusion
If you like shop management sims with a lot of min/maxing, dungeon crawling, and the never-ending grind of leveling with a fun, addicting backdrop, this is a great game for you.
Just be aware you'll be in it for the long haul.

Please note that this review is solely based off of the first impressions I had in the first 2 and a half hours after played this title, and despite the "early access" label this game has been given, will give my thoughts on the current build, that being dated on July 3rd 2016.
The idea of piloting a zepplin in a majorly steampunk universe with the goal of providing commerce to the towns of this seemingly expansive world appealed greatly to me. As such, I decided to dive blindly into this game to see what it offered.
For the most part, the game looks relatively pretty, despite the moderately low texture resolution, even on the highest graphics settings offered. Ship models look very nice, and for the most part, control as expected, if not just a little clunky at times. The only real complaint I have with the graphics is anti-aliasing. Shadows for this game need serious improvement for a day-night cycle system this game has.
For an airship game, the controls, as I said before, operate as expected, but I found them to be rather spread out. To control the ship, for example, you use the arrow keys instead of the traditional WASD bindings. While this normally wouldn't be a complaint from me, you're forced to use your mouse in order to not only drag the screen, but to also select objects. And without, from what I've been able to see so far, an ability to change keybindings to something more comfortable, you can't do much. You can, however, use the mouse solely to not only control your ship, but other options as well. Problem is, with a game that totes the ability to explore, I'd much rather control the ship with button controls rather than click a location and go from there. To me, it's not very feasible at the current moment.
The gameplay itself is rather confusing as well. According to what I've seen on my HUD, there's supposed to be a leveling system. However, I've been unable to figure out how to successfully level up. There's no clear indication on how to level, nor is there a tutorial on what to do in order to do so. I figured the progression would be something like this: Get contracts from a port ---> navigate and deliver said contracts to the appropriate location ---> Obtain rewards and gain experience to raise your level. Basically typical MMORPG leveling. Because it isn't clear in this regard, I've been thus far unable to figure it out. Everyone in chat I've talked to has said to look at the guides on Steam to get an idea as to what to do. Problem is, and I can't really stress this enough, a player SHOULD NOT have to look to an outside source to learn about BASIC FUNDAMENTALS OF A GAME. This should be something in the game ITSELF that's explained, guides outside should explain more complicated stuff, not basic things.

Valkyria Chronicles is an amazing strategy game. However there are many other genres at work here as well. You can call this game a hybrid between a strategy game, a third person shooter, a visual novel and an RPG.
And the great part about this game is that it does not sacrifice the depth of one genre for the sake of another.They come together beautifully to form a really great experience.They also made a great choice with the art style, this is a game from 2008 and it looks just as good now as it did back then. The game looks good in all aspects of gameplay, the map overview, in third person, in visual novel parts and in the squad management screens.
What really hits home for me as well is the squad management aspect of the game. This includes everything from upgrading your weapons and armour, upgrading your tanks, ranking up your classes to managing who actually gets into your squad based on their traits and who they play best with. It's a deep system and it's really satisfying putting all the pieces into place before heading off into battle.
Most of the time you will be spending either following the story or doing the actual battles. The story is delivered as a visual novel (fully voice acted) or in cutscenes (although not as often), and it is intelligent enough to present to you the different points of view of the characters on opposing sides and interesting enough to hold your attention throughout. The battle system is probably where the game really shines, it is divided into two parts. First you have the map overview where you have represented everyone in your squad and every enemy they can see, from here you select one of your characters and you are switched to the second part. The third person action section, where you manually move the characters and aim their shots. You can take your time here as well, just be careful not to do it in front of an enemy as they will shoot at you if you enter their view cone.
Once in battle you have the option of controlling a tank or an infantry fighter from the 5 different classes in the game (scout, assault, lancer, engineer and sniper). Each of them have their own roles and usefulness, however I will say that some of the classes become less and less useful as the story progress. This is especially true for the sniper, as their very limited amount of action points means that you will not be able to effectively use them past the first few turns of the battle (and also the levels are designed so that there aren't many levels with completely open fields, there is always something in the way, or the enemies hunkered down and at that point a sniper can not one shot kill them even with a headshot). To a lesser extent this is also true for the lancers, as their primary role of being anti tank fighters is done just well by the actual tanks in your possession, and their similarly low amount of AP means that they're not that good at sneaking behind the enemy and shooting at the weak spots. The assault class can do this just as well, if you buff them they can take down a tank by shooting at their weak spot in one turn even, and on top of that they can retaliate on the enemy infantry (which the lancers can not, as they only have an anti tank weapon). As time goes on you will see what is truly useful to you and the great part is that you can build a squad however you want, there are only a few characters that you can not switch out of a squad going into battle.
The biggest drawback is that everything just moves too slowly in the game. When you're in a position where you just want to move up all of your guys, you have no choice but to manually take control of each of them and slowly run forward and in the later stages of the game that means moving 10 characters each turn. It can get annoying fast, but thankfully there aren't too many of those instances as usually you will have at least someone to fight along the way.
And there is something similar for the story part, if it's not an actual cutscene, then you have to manually move the text forward. I would like to just sit back and enjoy the story as it goes, but it becomes annoying having to press space after every single sentence, to the point that I stopped listening to the characters and just reading what they're saying and skipping as soon as I could. Definitely not the right way to enjoy the story, but they really should have put an option there to automatically skip once a character is done speaking.
I will also mention that the map overview section would really need some additional info displayed on it, things like effective range of your characters and the enemies, and view cones for all the characters. There has been too many times that I lost a character by entering the edge of the view cone of an enemy, this is difficulty by obfuscation not by clever design. And there are also other small annoyances which help keep the game from being truly amazing.
All in all Valkyria Chronicles is truly amazing, and the type of game that we're lucky to get on the PC. I remember seeing this game back in 2008 when it was released for the PS3 and just knowing that there is something special about it, I'm just happy to be able to play it now on the PC, even if it is almost a decade later. It is also packed with content, it will take you around 30 hours to finish the game, and then you can go on to new game plus or you can do some of the challenges.

I enjoyed Mass Effect 1 but was only able to give it 3/5 due to some pretty annoying flaws. I’m glad to say that most of those flaws have been eradicated in ME2. Gone are the endless slow elevator rides. Gone are the tedious, bouncy buggy rides on dull, lifeless planets. And gone is the ridiculously complex HUD. What hasn’t changed are its strong points, which remain in the storyline and RPG elements. Once again there is a detailed and compelling story along with many side plots and missions, which are more diverse and creative than those in ME1. The voice acting is excellent throughout as are the character models and animations, which are fluid and naturalistic. Graphically it’s very good for a four-year-old game, although there’s little in the way of physics, which is a shame. The combat has also improved, although it remains rather clunky and lacklustre compared to other games. The Mass Effect franchise is clearly about providing a rich and developed universe in which to place the player and to give that player a full-bodied RPG experience peppered with combat and action along the way. And in this respect ME2 really delivers. If not for the so-so combat I would have given it 5/5, but as it is I give it 4/5.

It's been said, but this game has alot of potential.  Unlike many Early Access games, this game is amazingly lacking in bugs.  Where it does lack, however, is in content.  The world this game takes place in is ENORMOUS; and everything is in real-time.  If one wanted to travel from one side of the world to the other it would actually take an entire day.  Although that is impressive, I excpected to rewarded by my adventurous nature and find better trade opportunities, equipment, and jobs; this is not the case and from what I have found it is opposite.  Right now there is no reason for the player to venture outside of the safety zone of the captial city and it's immediate outlying settlements because, other than scenary, there is no advantage to doing so.  The trade and job systems need alot of balancing as the value in involving yourself in either is not profitable unless you commit yourself to several weeks of performing non-stop monotonous tasks.  I'm disappointed that I've put in as many hours as I have in this game (99% travel time where I could literally walk away from the computer and come back several hours later to continue what I had planned), but it really does appear promising; just dont expect a ton of gameplay value yet. For you readers who want to get down to the point (more details below);
Yes – I can only recommend it. If you already enjoyed ETS2 or anything else along those lines, this simulator will be right down your alley.
Admittedly, there is a lack of variety in the trucks as well as the settings, especially in the southern part of the map as it is mostly desert. Additionally, it will always get compared to ETS2 and at the moment, it will lose that comparison. Nonetheless, good buy. 8/10
Getting into more details now;
Firstly, let me address some of the concerns raised by other players.
“Traffic doesn’t stop at red lights”
I had to read up on this because it confused me as well in the beginning. Unlike Europe – if a traffic light is red in the US, right turns can still be made if the road is clear. I do not know if this is an obvious fact but I only found out about this now.
“Map is too small / Plays like an add-on”
Currently I am on the fence about this statement. On the one hand, 2 trucks and (currently) two states is a bit little especially if you are used to ETS and its expansions. This is not really helped by the fact that the map lacks some variety - being green and lush in the northern part of the map and desert in the south with not much variation in between. No one was expecting a “The Crew” style map with all of the US on it but maybe one more state (Oregon / Idaho) in the basic pack for a more diverse map would have helped.
On the other hand though, the trucking takes time again in between cities, especially on the long hauls and it is fun. Personally, I also like the fact that there seems to be a better feel for the size of cities by being actually able to drive in and through some of the bigger cities. Again though, it’s all in proportion. I will not be able to have 100’s of streets for LA but a couple that make it feel like I am actually in a city.
However, for (in the UK) £14.99 I cannot really complain about the price. Let’s see how much the inevitable add-ons will be.
“Harsh fines / Erratic AI behaviour”
So far, I can confirm this. I have found myself more often than I like to admit paying fines for ‘speeding’ by doing 57mph when the limit was 55mph. Also, on more than one occasion - especially in the cities - the AI seems not to properly recognize the trailer and drives straight into it, leaving me with a hefty fine. Especially at the beginning this is quite painful as the fines quickly add up to thousands of US$.
“Performance issues”
For me, the game runs surprisingly smooth. In fact, it actually runs better for me than ETS2, especially when the truck lights are on. In ETS2 a lot of players had drops in framerates when turning on the headlights or in tunnels, this issue seems to be resolved here.
The only problem I have encountered is that the game itself is incredibly dark. If had to put the brightness setting almost to the max to actually see something during the night and in bad weather.
“Highways in the US have more than 2 – 3 lanes”
Although this may be true it has to be seen in relation. The volume of the cars has already noticeably increased and makes the game feel much livelier. I do not know if this does impact the performance of the game for some players but I can only imagine that if there is an 8 lane highway around LA it will make it unplayable. Additionally, the sections that are so huge would need to be incredibly short as they only appear in metropolitan areas whereas 90% of the map is set in a rural environment, highway wise I mean.
Secondly, some of my observations
- Really enjoy the introduction of the weighting stations. They add some much needed realism to the game. However, they do not seem to do anything other than stopping your drive for a short while. I wonder if there is the possibility (or random occurrence) of getting fined for overloading or something along those lines.
- Road construction sites are back on. Question is if they are random occurrences or static set pieces.
- Traffic volume has been set a lot higher. Finally it feels like driving at rush hour and less like on an oversized motorway where I am the only driver.
- Little touches here and there that make the game feel livelier. Eg; trucks and cars pulling into petrol stations and stopping at the pumps.
- A really nice setting with a lot of new details and set pieces. They could have easily reused a lot of old décor from ETS2 but it all seems to be newly build and really captures the atmosphere of the US
- Again though, some of the highway connections are just odd. Why are there a couple of highways where there could have been a highway junction but instead I have to get onto a country road from one highway to join the next literally a couple of (ingame) yards away.
However, as mentioned above, I can only recommend it. Being the spiritual successor of ETS2 and having not yet reached the same size, it will lose all comparisons. It has to be said that ETS2 also does not give us all of Europe (south of Italy or West France, Spain & Porugal) but due to mods most is now possible and the expansions, although pricey, were always worth it. I hope that the pricing policy for this game will not be exorbitant as the developers have done a great job but I equally will not fork out £10 fifty times over to get all States – if this will ever happen.
It could do with some tweaks but it looks very promising so far which is why I have no regret buying this game and can only recommend it to anyone who like a good simulation. 8/10

I've never written a Steam review before, but really wanted to sing the praises of this game.
I'm someone who loves to drive in real life, and who also comes from and lives in California. I'm a fan of EuroTruck Simulator 2 (and I also lived in the UK for 5 years), but felt a lot of the scenery and layout was very repetitive and would often uninstall after only a few play sessions, although I'd reinstall it once in awhile. Solid game tho, and the business tycoon style aspect was fun.
In American Truck Simulator you really have the same game however I strongly feel they've done a fantastic job of skinning the game in such a way that really gives the feeling and spirit of the American Southwest very well. I know and have driven many times around the places in this game and while it's not 100% perfect or to scale, there's a ton of subtleties that this game gives to very much put you in something a lot like real life.
The windmills off Highway 111 (down in what is effectly the Coachella Valley, where Palm Springs is), the tree barriers found off Highway 99 that runs along the eastern side of the San Juaqin Valley (which is very different to the feel of the 5 Freeway which runs down the west side of that huge valley), the way the roads and buildings change while you drive over the Sierra Nevada pass (past Truckee) and into Nevada itself. The way the roads work around Las Vegas. All of these examples and hundreds more really give you a strong sense of what it is to drive around this part of the world, with all of the other successful elements from EuroTruck Simulator 2, including the ability to customize your music, and even just use preexisting Internet Radio streams which are all highly appropriate, to managing your own company of trucks and drivers over time.
Getting better in the game requires coming to learn what different areas of the map will throw at you to slow you down or trip you up, eg parts of a freeway being subject to harsh speed limits (and getting a huge speed fine if you miss it) or understanding that making a left onto a freeway from a country lane could take you an extra half an hour, or knowing when sharp grades are better driven around than attempted head on, all of these things are at play and create a real sense of accomplishment over time as you begin to master the routes.
This is a very fun game that's just as good as its predecessor but I think a much more realistic and engaging experience than Euro 2. The only complaint I have is some minor AI issues that can occur around some intersections and a funny thing where some intersections have both stop lights and stop signs too which seem to confuse the AI (and also isn't how America traffic works either). It's a pretty minor problem though that may even disappear someday.
Defininte recommend for anyone who liked the predecessors.

Crusader Kings II is a typical paradox games. Paradox excell at making games that you can essentially play forever. Extremely similar to Europa Universalis III, this title is even better if you ask me.
It's very difficult to review a paradox game. What makes it great? In truth, the game is very simple. You have a map, you have some functions and an interface. Apart from Heroes of Might and Magic, what other title has ever gotten anything right with these few tools? Well Crusader Kings certainly has.
Diplomacy, strategy and patience. This game is a challenge for most people, and the challenge isn't winning, because you cannot win this game, the challenge is accepting your losses and your failures.
What you do in Crusader Kings is essentially attempting to re-write history as you please, but without severely lowering the difficulty or cheating, it often feels like trying to run away from someone in a dream. It's often completely futile and it's as if there was a reason things went down the way they did! Funny that.
Changing history is hard, and this game will show you why. The game will also make you view women as a resource to expand your power, and view men as potential competitors. You will learn to trust no-one and it will teach you the painful lesson that Muslim rulers always have another son or a cousin or someone with an equally silly hat to take their palce if you have them executed.

Ambitious. Bugged. Beautiful. Cluttered. Revisionist. Old School. Historically-inaccurate. Ultimately...flawed.
This is a game that I wanted to love -- that I still want to love. But unfortunately it's flaws are both asthetic and mechanical, and lamentably myriad. EG: The game crashes when you try to return to the main menu, and it does so every single time. No matter how well-trained and well-equipped, your units will ALWAYS perform poorly, while enemy units will always perform with expert precision (even if unarmed, outnumbered, and incapacitated). It wants to push very particular 21st century political reinterpretations of the era of the Conquistadores, but it does so while simultaneously pretending that 15th-16th century Spain was an egalitarian culture in which men and women alike served in the military, in academia, etc. Kind of hard to push the "EVIL-WHITE-MEN-RUINED-PRISTINE-PERFECT-UTOPIAN-PRE-COLOMBIAN-AMERICA" narrative when you're presenting the conquistadores as a gender-and-racial-inclusive 21st-century-style group to satisfy the tastes of modern, historically-illiterate players... Etc. etc. etc. What you wind up with is a game that looks lovely, and is full of potential, but which is all the more frustrating and disappointing because of that. Its flaws make its merits into flaws, since they highlight what might have been and emphasize how far short the programmers fell of their apparent goals. I'd give this a pass. It'll only break your heart (and drive you bonkers if you're a historian).

This is exactly what it says on the tin. It's a Disgaea game.
Like all Disgaea games, we've got an incredible soundtrack, pretty in-depth combat system, levels and damages into the millions, etc, etc. All par for the course here.
But for those who are not familiar with this series... Let's break it down:
In-depth combat system, in the style of any "tactics" jRPG, such as Fire Emblem or FF Tactics, except with a ton more piled on top, such as colored panels and stones, which you can maniuplate to change buffs/effects present on the battlefield.
Your party is entirely up to you, you're given several story characters to use, with their unique abilities, but you can choose to use them or not, on top of those, you can also create your own characters, "rebirth" them into various classes, and customize all of their equipment.
Your characters level up and gain abilities, like any good RPG game would have, but your abilities also gain levels based on on how much you use them. Which let's you even further customize your characters by raising certain abilities.
You can also level up your items by battling inside of "item world" and change the various stat growths on each item, on top of leveling it up.
The soundtracks of Disgaea are simply amazing, and the game knows it, as you can buy the soundtracks and change where each track plays by default, to customize even the music you listen to while you play the game.
You can really change up the game by passing a bill, at the dark assembly, which is essentially a democratic vote in the demon world. You can raise your influence by bribing the voters... Or just make it pass, by force. Doing this, you can change the difficulty of enemies, create incredibly powerful characters, and change various other aspects of the game.
Tired of playing games and only getting to level 99? Because Disgaea doesn't care in the SLIGHTEST about such puny caps.
You want ridiculous levels, and damages exceeding hundreds of millions? This is your game.
Completely ridiculous, and amazingly chaotic.
And finally, I want to address the fact that this game is a port, and as such it suffers from many problems.
Problems inclue SAOO completely destroying the graphics with black fuzz all over.  Easily fixed by just turning it off.
Mouse controls do not respond very well when trying to open menus or give units orders. I'd recommended you play with a controller or keyboard to avoid this, but not required, as the mouse controls are reliably awkward, and after a few battles, you'll be able to play using a mouse without any issues.
Some people report performance issues even on high-end systems.. I've not experienced any of these issues, but I have looked into them, the developers are fully aware of them, and are working to resolve them. So worry not, fixes are coming!
At the end of this, I would give this game an 8/10, fix the problems and I'd say 9/10.  Highly recommended, to returning fans, and new players alike.

As a life-long fan of the Disgaea series, I anxiously awaited the PC debut. A chance to play it again, steam achievements, and the possibility of series support on my platform of choice?! Sign me up, Dood!
Then, news of a high-profile gaming website slamming the port as "shoddy" and "unacceptable" started to circulate. I became nervous, and worried that NISA had dropped the ball and doomed my favorite series before it even properly released. Will it be unplayable? Are the graphics options all screwed up? Will it control terribly? I decided to wait patiently for my preorder to unlock and test it myself...
I am happy to report that none of the issues that article reported exist, in my experience. It appears, from doing some research, that the problems reported are entirely random and/or isolated instances that may be due to optimization conflicts. What does that mean to you, review-reader? Well, you could have a perfect experience like I have had thus far: solid 60FPS, zero screen tearing, wonderful mouse response (playing Disgaea with a mouse was something I NEVER expeected to enjoy, but here I am not even hooking up my controller!), and wonderful audio quality. Or you could have less-than-perfect performance, some of which is solveable with a few tweaks on your end. NISA has started collecting data from users who are experiencing issues, so hopefully all of that will be solved in short-order.
Now, this isn't without a few words of warning: some of the new settings are, quite frankly, garbage. Blurring the edge of the screen? PASS! Blurring the characters so that they don't look like their original pixel art style? No way, Dood! Personally, I really like the new (HD) menu style, and the enhanced map graphics. The fact that you have the option to toggle ALL of the changes is fantastic, and I'm glad that NISA realized that the PC community likes to customize their experiences individually.
If you're interested in a classic Strategy RPG (this is a port of the PSP version, a decade old, of a game that originally released on the PS2 in 2003) that shows a bit of age, but hasn't lost an ounce of the brilliant humor and tactics that made it the cult hit that it was, do yourself a favor and check out Disgaea PC. I can't recommend it enough, and I really hope that the rest of the series begins to make it to Steam in the future. Get out there and get your Overlord on!

Note: Summary at the bottom of the review.
Ace Patrol is the first of the (currently two) Ace Patrol games. While its successor tackles WW2, this takes on WW1 where the strategy involves maneuvering your plane into the best possible position to shoot down the enemy. As you progress, nev maneuvers, planes and improvements become avaliable. The game is a casual one, but while you cannot expect much depth or complexity from it, you can expect it to be a fun pack-up-and-play game. And in all honesty, how many WW1 Air Combat TBS games are there out there? The originality of it alone deserves mention!
Another thing that should be mentioned is that your squadron will have female combat pilots. While I applaud the inclusion of female pilots on the principle of it being awesome, I am puzzled why Firaxis neglected to include an option to disable them for those that want to preserve some historical accuracy.
Pro:
*Fun little TBS air-combat game.
*Includes female pilots, yay!
*Casual pick-up-and-play style.
Con:
*Lacking in depth and complexity.
*No option to turn off female pilots for those wanting historical accuracy.
*Not a lot of customization when it comes to graphics, etc.
Summary:
Ace Patrol is worth its asking price, so long as you do not expect a great amount of depth, complexity or historical accuracy. That being said, it is a fun game set in a very interesting era of aviation! 5/10 -Recomended.

The game has a lot of customizing to it, with nameable pilots, colourable planes and of course, new planes that become available gradually. Your pilots are customizeable in the way of promotions and special medals, which allow them to learn new moves like Power maneauvers, Slide, Roll as well as a number of special Ace skills.
It's a fairly short game but i still found it very entertaining.

This game has some nice things, like graphics, sound, and mods that don't ban you for foul language.  Unfortunately, thats the positives.
The game is awful.  To get anywhere in the game, you must grind a lot.  But, you're restricted by labour, an alternate game currency that slows you down from completing things quickly.  You need labour for pretty much everything.
You must also farm (which uses labour) and spend probably 1 hour a day just doing that, and thats before you're off doing dungeons or trading or piracy.
I really tried to like the game, but Trion are way more interested in you spending money in their shop than fixing anything, like the many bugs in the game.

Bought this on a whim... Sat down to play and woke up a couple of days later having just experienced one of the best stories in my gaming life. From the art style, through the magnificent music and voice acting and to the sublime gameplay, this title oozes a level of polish that is lacking in this genre.
Now, I'm not normally a fan of JRPG's but this really took a hold of me with its alternative WW2 setting and really makes you think about human nature with its wonderfully written story.
Recommend? Absolutely, though not just  because you can make an all girl team... It's a game that, maybe on the surface at least, doesn't look all that interesting but rewards those who continue with an experience they'll never forget. Easily one of, it not THE best tactical RPG ever made.
Thank you SEGA for bringing this to Steam and please port the second game as well. There're fans waiting.

I'm currently midway through my second campaign, and words cannot describe how much I have loved this game.
However, I shall try!
I picked up this game during the summer sale for an almost criminally low price, but it's more than worth it's full cost to the right gamer. When debating getting the game, most of the reviews I read said things along the lines of "like Fire Emblem but with guns". Fire Emblem being my favourite series, this interested me considerably. The gameplay is turn based, but when units are selected, the battle becomes real time, allowing you to move soldiers around dodging enemy fire and finding good hiding spots from which to fell foes. This combination of two strategy game types works surprisingly well and allows you to see the fights from a commander and soldier perspective, which really helps you get immersed in the game.
Story-wise, the tale is set in 1935 on a continent not unlike Europe, between two warring superpowers; the Federation and the Imperials. On the border of these giants is a small country called Gallia, which has remained neutral in the conflict. However, all machinery (both military and otherwise) in this world is powered by a mineral called Ragnite, which Gallian soil holds in abundance, prompting the Imperials to invade. You play as Welkin Gunther, son of a legendary war hero, and members of Squad 7 as you undertake critical missions to push back the invasion and win your freedom!
The events of the story really got to me in some places, both elated moments and tragic ones. This game really takes your emotions for a ride when it wants to!
Music-wise, there is almost no fault to be had anywhere, except that there is not more of it! The different melodies perfectly reflect the scenarios they pair with, and I often found myself extra happy when a tune I liked began.
Overall, this game is one of the best I've ever played, and I heartily recommend it to others, especially if strategy games are your thing.

Hidden Object Bundle 5 in 1 is a collection of five hidden object games. In chronological order, it was the first appearance of each game on Steam. However, Weird Park Trilogy was released (containing Weird Park: Broken Tune), Mountain Crime: Requital followed as a stand-alone before Twisted Land Trilogy finally arrives.
You're investigating the disappearance of a journalist in an abandoned fair park. However, a little gnome seems to prevent you to discover what happened... because everything seems tied to the death of Louis Gauche, a clown that lost his life during a representation... Besides, you'll find scattered around parts of a music disk, what is it meaning?
Here's what I wrote about the game in my Weird Park Trilogy review:  I enjoyed the dark settings and the soundtrack. But I had an hard time to find my way sometimes, relaying on the hint buttons. Besides, the ending was promising a real good sequel.
Indeed, Weird Park: Broken Tune is my favorite game from the bundle because of its unique atmosphere. The graphics were reflecting the fact that something bad happened and that paranormal activity was perhaps also involved. The gameplay was well-balanced too.
For more information about Weird Park Trilogy, I suggest you to read my review:
You're called by a patient of yours to an hotel build on the ashes of a children hospice that suffered a tragedy. However, customers began dying... and they're all tied to that tragedy...
The game was my second favorite from the bundle, though I found a little longer and though the gameplay is different from the others, as you're gathering items in a scene that you need to build an object for an action.
As I've already reviewed the game and that I fear that copying/pasting it here will make me reach a characters limit for the review, I prefer to give you the link to it:
After a problem in the middle of the sea, you end up in a strange town, with your wife being dragged by an unknown man. What terrible secret will you uncover?
I must admit that while I enjoyed another somber story (the game is during the night, in a foggy town, with many mysteries around), I was quite confused about it. Given the twist at the end, I thought that it was a second opus in a series. In reality, it is really the first in the trilogy.
Here's an extract of my Twisted Land Trilogy review: The plot of the first game is perhaps basic but with all the questions arising during your quest and the fact you're seeing ghosts, you bet that there is a dark cult under it. Though the end tells you how Mark came on the Island, which is a shocking twist, playing it a second time had made more understanding of the story than the first time. The graphics are correct, the soundtrack is also too, but the problem is that you're doing a lot of backtracking for an object.
For more information about the trilogy, read my review:
After defeating a witch, she's ready to take revenge on you through your innocent son. Will you manage to save his soul?
I was quickly bored with this game. Given the fact that it was a direct sequel to another game, I felt like I was missing something. Based on the same gameplay of Mountain Crime, I didn't really enjoy it - I played Behind the Reflection 2 before Mountain Crime. The items weren't easy to find, though the puzzles were well-balanced.
The graphics were correct, though the soundtrack didn't let me a memory.
Why is your grandfather hiding a young girl and seems scared of her? What happened in his past? Did he really meet vampires?
The plot is alternating between the present and the past of your grandpa. It means that you're alternating between a cosy house and an old boat. And that game, while not being a total disaster, is the worst in the bundle. I found it very ridiculous, some dialogues are coming from uninspired minds and it becomes a parody of some sorts. It wasn't always easy to find your way around. The graphics were correct, that's true, but it does not save the game in my eyes. I really wondered why this joke was put in a bundle
I really enjoyed that bundle, well, at least for 3 games. I can't say that the two other games weren't appreciated but I was quickly bored with them, even if I got an hard time with Twisted Land. The question is: should you buy the bundle when three of them are on Steam, with Twisted Land and Weird Park being in their trilogy and with Mountain Crime being a stand-alone? If I had written the review earlier, I would have say that you had to buy it. However, now, the bundle could be seen as not worthy.
In reality, for the price, it's worthy to buy it and to try at least Twisted Land and Weird Park. Indeed, their trilogy are nearly 20 euros while the bundle is half the price. I will admit something: it's because I've played them in the bundle that I bought the two trilogies nearly at their release.  Else I would have activated them from a bundle or would have waited for a discount. As for Mountain Crime in my library, the reason is called "trading cards" and "badge". The two other games are only on Steam in this bundle.
I will not change my mind: Hidden Object Bundle 5 in 1 is still a bundle of five games and is still worthy of any purchase. True, for those already owning the three games through the trilogies and the stand-alone game, the bundle isn't at all interesting. For the others, it's still a good bargain, at least, you will know if you like Twisted Land and Weird Park and if buying the trilogies could be a future action.

Disclaimer: I had already played through this quite a bit on the PS3 version before I bought it, so I had a pretty decent idea what I was getting into when I bought this.  From a porting standpoint, I feel like they did a great job aside from tank steering randomly getting buggy at times.
Story: (that's why we play RPGs...right?)
The story is very character-driven, which I personally love but that's not necessarily for everyone.  You will gain an irrational attachment to some characters after using them in a few missions and they all have their unique quirks and personalities.  The unfortunate thing about this is pretty much everyone in your squad isn't developed in the great way the main cast is.  It makes sense to be that way since every single member of your squad is optional aside from the core characters, but I can't help but think the story would be even more immersive if you could find out about the supporting cast aside from their bios.  I'd rate the story a good 9/10 on the enjoyment scale.
Gameplay:
I've loved tactical RPGs since playing Final Fantasy Tactics on the PS1.  The gameplay doesn't present anything that would disappoint someone that likes turn-based strategy games.   It might be a little on the easy side, but it is engaging, fun, and has reasonable replay value to it.  My only complaint for gameplay is the way the mission ranking system works.  Revolving only around the total number of turns it takes to complete the mission objectives somewhat encourages abandoning actual tactical movements in favor of abusing system mechanics. Orders are REALLY strong and in a lot of cases the most straightforward way to get an A-rank is just mindlessly buff a unit (Alicia OP) and have them run through enemy lines by themselves while effectively incincible.  Oh, and almost never move/use your tanks unless the objective is to get a tank somewhere.
In a realistic war scenario, even if you somehow sneak into and take a base surrounded by enemies...one person alone isn't going to hold that base, and the enemy isn't going to simply retreat because one person is a mile away from the rest of their unit holding that base.  I feel like this would be improved if the enemy ace / tanks / commanders killed played into more than just how much exp/gold you get from the mission.  Taking out an ace or disabling an extra five tanks would help the war quite a bit in normal circumstances.
Gameplay itself 10/10
Ranking system 5/10
Music:
The soundtrack is solid and helps keep you immersed in the story. 8/10
TL;DR - If you're a fan of turn-based strategy games, character-driven stories, or just cute girls killing things, this game is for you.

This game is a card game.  It is a resource management game.  It is a brawler. It is a text based, classic adventure game. It is a RPG and a rogue-like. This game is phenomenal, I thoroughly enjoyed my short time with it so far.
I played but just 1 hour of Hand of Fate, I closed the game and instantly came to write this piece.  If you are like me and you like a good RPG, choose your own adventure or anything vaguely close to fantasy, I feel you will appreciate the direction that this game embarked upon.
Hand of Fate handles the tutorial with such finesse that I wasn’t even aware it was a tutorial until it had come to a end – I was already invested In my character and in my story.
When you first boot up the game it will launch you directly in to the “game of life and death”, as is so aptly described by the card dealer. You will proceed to get comfortable at the fortune teller-esque table and Gothic surroundings with a inexplicably cryptic figure who welcomes you to the game of life and death. We do not know who the card dealer is, but you will get a sense of power and mystique as he shuffles the deck. Very quickly you will come to realise that Hand of Fate is not a run-of-the-mill card game, it is that and so much more.
The premise is to advance through each area and kill the twelve different heroes, that are under the guidance of the quippy card dealer.  The dealer will lay several cards in front of you on to a table, where you will take control of a game piece, just like in a board game. To advance you must move the game piece on to the different cards and watch the game unfold, for every card you move to one piece of food will be consumed – manage these resources very carefully. Each card brings with it its own adventure and riches, its own danger and fortunes, will you be brave and save the Captain of the Guard or leave him to the fate of the Undead?
Defeating a hero card can be rewarding and in some cases, difficult.  With them, hero cards draw different monster cards from the deck that will place them in to the battle, increasing its difficulty. Once a hero is defeated, the game is over and you will be able to use any card tokens that you obtained throughout your journey to unlock more cards.
Unlocking cards will allow you to customize your deck to your liking, just like any other collectible card game. If you are not in to fiddling about with so many cards, or are inexperienced with creating card decks, there is a option to create a deck optimized for you – Which the game will do for you.
The tone is set from the exact moment you launch the game – it is dark, it is mysterious and it is Gothic. The art direction for this title is spot on, everything just fits in to place, even the cards are designed in such an intricate way they left me feeling that I was really sitting at the table playing this game. The burning candle flickering over the game table sets the perfect mood for a stare-down with a hooded, mystic figure. I would love to be able to buy myself a physical copy of the cards.
I genuinely cared for the actions that I took.  I wanted to save the Captain of the Guard, I wanted to loot the goblin cave and plunder its riches and I felt it necessary to make a deal with the devil. I delved in to reading each card and the tales it brought with it.  My hero was a holy-mace wielding, bandit slaying, guard saving badass and I loved it. I wanted to make sure that he had the gear I wanted him to have; maybe not necessary the best gear, but the gear that I believed fit in to his persona. This was a pen and paper RPG at its finest.
Did I mention that this game is a brawler?  No?  Well it is.  When the cards are down and the candle flickers, when playing the game of life and death and inhaling the musky atmosphere, expect to kill or be killed. Combat is not turn based – It is not handled like a card game nor is it RPG-like.  I would forgive you for thinking that combat happens like that of a text-based adventure game, but you would be wrong. You, your character and all of the gear you have amassed will be teleported in to a 3D environment along with the monster cards that were drawn, and you will fight.  Combat is much like the Arkham series, but feels less polished.  It is obvious that this was not meant to be the games strong point – And that is okay.  It works and It fits in with the game, hell, at this point what doesn’t?
Within 1 hour of gameplay I had created a character that I was entirely invested in and cared about. He had saved the Captain of the Guard who provided us with his powerful Mace masked in a Holy boon to ward off the Undead. I had met a Fair Maiden who blessed me with life longevity by providing me with a +5 health boost. I encountered Mister Lionel, a Goblin disguised as a old man who mysteriously appeared a shield right in front of my face, as a gift. I had scaled the winding vines of a canyon as a glistening metal caught my eye – I had found a sword. The Maze Of Traps had been conquered and the gold plundered. I defeated the Devil’s challenge before looting a Dead King’s Tomb for +10 Max health, food and riches. I was no longer playing as a character in a video game, I was me and I was creating a story.
Hand of Fate is fantastic and if you have a vested interest in RPG’s, card games or fantasy I highly suggest that you give this game a go.  It is something different that tries and succeeds in covering many different game genres. This game is a gem that I was not expecting, I had no idea that this game was being released and I am glad I paid a measly £15 for this phenomenal title.  I know for certain I have only scratched at the surface of this game and I need to get back to playing more.

-A must play with friends. Sure, that's pretty much the same with any MMO, but if you're looking for the most fun out of the f2p model, then a large group of friends who are available are a must have (a group of 4s is recommended, but you can stick it out with just 3 or 2)
-If you're heading in on your own, be forewarned, PVP is ingratuitously unfair to either underleveled or unpaying members.
Those are the only bad things I can really say about the game. There are people who complain about how you have to pay for permanent items, but those items are purely aesthetic, as your gear is permanent, albeit not the most pleasant to look at, but at least it actually changes when you equip something new. The game is fast-paced, rewarding for leveling up, and incredibly customizable with the skills you get. Also, you're given a gratuitous amount of character slots for just f2p, and buying more only seems necessarry if you REALLY want to have either A: all the characters (which are so vastly different, that you might just try them out, decide that you don't like them and pick a different one until you have a cast you like) or B: another of the same character, but dramatically recustomized into a different subclass.
tl;dr It's a mostly fair (outside pvp) f2p game that I wouldn't mind putting money into just for the extra character slots. Get some friends together, and try it out if you have the chance

Right off the bat I will say that if you’re a fan of hidden object games then this is a great bundle for you. You get five games for a great low price and each one offers something different.
A game you can buy and play separately on Steam now in a bundle. Your character is a doctor that was invited to a hotel to treat someone but things start to go terribly wrong. There is a snow storm, dead bodies galore and an ending that will either shock you or down right make you laugh. It’s not the best story but I found enjoyable for the sheer absurdity of it all.
The game play is a little different from other hidden object games. The hidden object scenes are not aimless clicking for a list of items, you’re actually looking for important pieces making each scene fit better into the storyline itself. The art is dated but not bad, the voice acting his laughable and the soundtrack is fitting. While not a masterpiece it was my favorite out of the five.
My second favorite of the bundle and another game you can purchase on its own on Steam. I found it to be insanely creepy but that’s because I highly dislike clowns. The story isn’t too creepy, though. You play a detective investigating a series of deaths at an amusement park. Once there you find out there is more than meets the eye as the park is haunted by a ghost clown and Loki.
The game play is very basic, good ole fashioned hidden object scenes along with challenge mini games and puzzles. The artwork is fitting for the dark atmosphere mixed with unsettling music as well. The voice acting is nothing to write home about but the game is good enough where that doesn’t matter. This game is the first in a trilogy which you can also find on Steam.
I liked this game, it wasn’t amazing in any way but I enjoyed playing it. This is the first in a trilogy which you can purchase on Steam and the name is very fitting. The game starts off simply enough, you’re on a boat with your wife after you just went diving on treasure until things go awry and and you find your boat in shambles and your wife missing while you’re on an unknown island. Everything else is pretty confusing. You keep seeing ghosts, clues you find point in different directions, there really is no clear danger at all until the very end and there is no interactions whatsoever. I did like the ending, though, I saw it coming but I still liked it.
The game has fun hidden object scenes as well as puzzles and mini games. The game doesn’t try to reinvent the wheel. You can get through the game in one sitting, it’s not very long or involved but still enjoyable. The art is alright, not the best. No voice acting but the music worked. It’s a very middle of the road game.
And now we get to the bottom rung games of the bundle. This game is not bad but it’s also not good. It’s a sequel to a game I did not play and is not on Steam, however, at the beginning they give you a brief run down of the first game. In this game the witch you put in jail before has escaped and returned for revenge by taking your son’s soul. You set off on a rather boring mission to find her, defeat her and save your son. The game has you going through portals to very weird lands and even different time periods as you chase after her all of which are kind of outlandish and seem to have very little to do with you or the witch aside from Salem.
The hidden object element of the game is a little different. Each time you look for an item it’s part of a puzzle, so you find pieces of armor that you need to put together for a skeleton or a windmill or a sword. Also mixed in are more traditional hidden object scenes as well as plenty of mini games. I didn’t have any issues with the game play, though some of the objects were hard to find just because of the artwork or where they were placed. No voice acting and the art is kind of meh, but not a bad game for a bundle.
Last but not least, my more disliked game in the bunch. Unfortunately I played this one first because I saw the word vampire and got excited. This is the first in a trilogy not available on Steam currently. I found the story to be utter garbage. You start of as Tyler who rushes to his grandfather’s house because there is some big trouble going on. Then you switch to playing grandpa as he retells his story of stowing away on a boat trying to get back to America. The crew dies and you’re trying to figure out why and it’s just not interesting. You save a girl name Laura and protect her from the likes of an evil mummy, yeah a mummy. The game doesn’t even mention vampires until right near the end. More happens but I don’t want to spoil it, I just didn’t like it.
Game play was another thing I did not like. Usually if the game plays well I can somewhat look past a bad story but this didn’t even get that right. There are plenty of hidden object scenes, you’ll be revisiting the same ones over and over and over again so don’t worry. There are barely any puzzles or mini games to help break up the monotony and there is a ton of back tracking with no map or easy teleport feature. I didn’t point this out in any other games because it wasn’t as big of an issue but in this game, the back tracking is super frustrating. No voice acting, probably for the best, and really drab music.
In my opinion you get two good games, two decent games and one bad game which isn’t a bad deal for the price.

I've gotten huge amounts of enjoyment out of this game.
It delivers in every area that it promises and if you are looking for a bordgameesque rougelike this is for you.
The game transitions from easy to very hard over the course of the game and there is little input from the player that can change the difficulty. For me this is not a problem as I enjoy the challenge, but for those looking for a game you can just walk through then you're probably not going to play to the end.
Something that came as a big and very welcome surprise was the storytelling. Which is told by the dealer who'll comment on everything that is happening. At first I thought that this was going to be off-putting after a while. But even now 30+ hours into the game I still want to hear everything he has to say. Through cryptic and vague pieces of information the story is revealed to you and it feels great to gather up these tidbits of information. The voice-acting is spot on and the amount of different monologues are huge.
As for gameplay there is a good balance between depth and simplicity. After a while you'll learn what encounter does what, but there is still a random element to each encounter that you as a player can influence. This lends to a big increase in replayability since even though you encounter the same stuff the outcomes will differ, and so will your experience during each playthrough.
The game looks good as well. While the graphics are not AAA they are certainly conveying the feelings that the atmospehere in this game needs to flourish. It also runs very well (at least on my computer).
Overall when it comes to atmosphere it's where this game shines the most. Thanks the combination of voiceacting and spot on artstyle you'll be drawn into the mysteries presented.
You'll want to see what waits ahead,
You'll want to push on further,
You'll want to find out what awaits in the end,
You'll want to understand.

This is truly a hidden gem.
The game had extremely humble beginnings - made by a circle of doujin developers (indie "indie") and aimed for only 10k sales outside Japan. Now this game has sold more than 300,000 copies. It's an unimaginable figure for a doujin title; it is more powerful than any review.
In this game you will get to manage an item shop found in many RPGs. You get to bargain with customers, upgrade the shop, acquire goods, etc. On top of that, you can also travel into classic RPG dungeons with hired adventurers to hunt for treasures. A game with more unique gameplay can scarcely be found. You don't have to enjoy anime-styled games to enjoy Recettear, but that can definitely be a plus too.
I highly recommend everyone to try the demo of this game. That should without a doubt convince you just how worthwhile it is to buy this game, with or without Steam sales.

-Unique card-based board game RPG with real time battles, fine idea and execution
One of the few good games that emerged from early access.
You face some mysterious card shark dude who also tells the story, does the tutorial and deals the cards.
You own two deck of items and encounter. The later become the playing field. You select some x cards of your card inventory to go into the story missions. The card man mixes some bad cards in. As you go the encounters are revealed, you sometimes have to fight in real-time and earn equipment, gold, food etc. Some encounters will give you new cards after the mission.
Opponents are also rendered from cards so a two of dust might be a two bandit fight. The fighting takes place in a small arena. You basically can attack, block and dodge roll with two optional cooldown powers depending on weapon and artefact equipment slot. Controls could be a little more responsive and some scenes I'd like to skip but those are real minor problems.
If you like say card based board games and fantasy RPG with a bit of hack and slash you shozuld really get the game as it is quite a new experience. Unlike the cover art the game has really atmosphere with your mysterious opponent who taunts you and tells stories.

I'm going to reccomend this game because it can be fun to some people. But very unfun if you dislike P2W, so please. Read on.
"Buy" the way, Free 2 Play games now a days cost more over time than AAA $60 games.
(I've probably spent over $2,000 in my 2 years in Elsword so far)
The game itself is fun. Graphics are light colorful and quircky. Sidescrolling beat em up. fun.
However the game is only fun if you have no sense or care of competetiveness at all. (Meaning you don't care about doing the most damage in dungeons and you don't care about winning PvP.)
The goods :
-Easy graphics, should run on almost any computer that has even the simplest of graphic cards.
-Easy to learn , fun to master. It's easy to get in the game and beat up monsters, then it's more fun to learn to do advanced tricks and moves with your character.
-Lot's of unique characters/class paths.
-Game is still young and growing (lot's of new content constantly coming out)
-Not much body costumization as you're playing set "characters", but looot's of outfits. The game is really good if you like to play dress up (note, yes it does cost real money to do so).
-Costumes have option to purchase permanent versions (more expensive but worth it)
-Costumes are tradable as long as you don't "take them out of the box (unseal them)", meaning lots of people buy and sell costumes from the item mall in the market for in-game money.
The bads :
- This game has an extreame P2W sickness. I've never seen a more P2W game than this. There is a character in the game, that if you put enough money into, can litterally one shot most other characters in PvP. And I mean litteral one shot. not 90%, not 99%. One shot one skill, you're dead, he wins. The freaking cosmetic costumes in this game are REQUIRED to get your stats higher.
- Item enhancments (the highest usually being +11, which can be bought through RNG durring +11 events) are carried over into PvP. Have fun in PvP if you like to play without pay.
- If you wind up in a party with a bunch of +11's while you only have a +7, you're going to feel completely USELESS. They'll most likely kill the mobs before you get to them.
-I can go on and on about P2W
-The game is young and growing (The level cap keeps going up, forcing you to keep buying  into +11 events to upgrade your equips if you like to stay competetive, new OP characters and classes keep coming out).
-You have to PAY to use more than 4 skills at once. When you start the game, there's 8 skill slots but 4 of them start locked, costing a whopping $8 to unlock them.
-The game lacks alot of social features, nothing much to do outside Raidboss, dungeons (which get boring after repeating them over and over) and PvP if you can stand it. Towns are usually silent as people don't have much reason to talk. I highly reccomend joining a guild if you need socialism.
Summary : If you're good at avoiding the trap which is "competetiveness" and can stick to just having fun, the game can be played with minimal spending (you're gonna want a costume). Game is heavily P2W. If you don't like spending money in order to keep up with everyone else, this isn't the game for you. If you like to play dress up with your characters though, this game can be fun still.

This game.... is bloody brilliant. Truly brilliant. I have little clue of who came up with some of these ideas, but if a dungeon crawler is your game, this is likely to make you re-assess your life choices. Meaning you shouldn't probably buy this or you will be here for hours. While some aspects are a tad flawed, for example some of the harsher penalties, they are welcomed except when recieved. In 2 bad double rolls 7 pain cards gave me 65 health lost permenantly, compared to 5 gold cards giving 100 or so gold. That concept alone should tell you how damning some of these choices can be, especially when the original card allowed 4 rolls and I failed only 2, when the odds are stacked 1 to 3, not in your favor.
The further the progres leads to more challenging cards, using the introductionary 5 bosses as an extended tutorial, and from there endless mode can be unlocked allowing for true replayability further down the line. As for those who find combat easy, they simply haven't had speed mods, curses, projectiles, and traps beating them down for a normal encounter. The difficulty does increase, that I assure neighsayers.
In all reality for 20 bucks I would buy it again, as it is probably one of the most original games I've played. Reminding me of the ever ending struggle against the game master. As for that game master? Probably one of the best cases of voice acting I've ever had the pleasure of working with. Funny enough I may embellish some aspects, but not by much, and truly worthwhile considering how often you have to deal with the snarky GM with the hands you on some occassion.
In short this game is bloody incredible, and I doubt I will stop playing it even after I obtain all of the achivements.

This game is far more fun and entertaining than I first thought when I got it. The idea is simplistic, 2d side scroller racing game, yet it has provided my friends and I hours of entertainment. It's great for LAN parties, where you can hear your friend rage at getting blown off the map by a bomb you set or being caught by your golden hook.
The good:
- Fun, fast paced gameplay
- Well balanced items. None of the items seems overpowered and there is a way to dodge most of them if youre quick.
- Wall jumping is well implemented and very smooth.
- Grappling hook is fun.
- Workshop level editor and the ability to play user created levels along with the official maps.
- Ranked and unranked matchmaking, as well as the ability to make custom lobbies
- Can use the keyboard (my preference) or game controller
Needs Improvement:
- Can be a bit glitchy sometimes, such as players teleporting through walls or floors, people winning when they weren't in first place sometimes, etc.
- If your or your opponents internet connection or connection to the server isn't great it can cause your oppenents to teleport around the screen
- Limited official maps. You go tend to memorize them pretty quickly.
- Having to buy some of the characters is annoying, but understandable I suppose. Would be nice to have the ability to unlock them through gameplay
- The single player campaign story is ok, but its kind of boring. Basically just a bunch of time trials (get to the bomb before it blows up) I don't have any ideas on how to make it better, but a little variety would go a long way.
- The bots can be kind of dumb sometimes, running off the screen in the wrong direction or getting stuck at a paticular point and not being able to move past it.
- The matchmaking needs a little work
- Sometimes the ranked matches don't record your points properly
Most of the "Needs Improvement" section is just nitpicky stuff that I'm sure will be cleared up by full launch. I really have nothing bad to say about the game, and woudl definitely recomend playing it. It's easy to learn, takes time to master some of the techniques and is great to play with friends. Easily worth $10. If you can shell out $70+ for a carbon copy fps every year you can afford to drop $10 on this great game.

If you're looking for a game review you've come to the wrong place. But if youre looking for a fantastic ravioli recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients
- To Make the Dough
375 grams (3 cups) plain flour
1/2 teaspoon salt
2 eggs
1/4 cup (50 ml / 3½ tablespoons) olive oil
1/2 cup (120 ml / 8 tablespoons) water
Extra flour for dusting
- To Make Cheese Filling
15 ounces (425 grams) container Ricotta cheese
5 ounces (142 g/about 1/2 cup plus 2 tablespoons) "3 Cheese Italian Blend" (Parmesan, Romano & Asiago)
Note: grate these cheeses yourself and create your own custom blend.
1/2 cup cheddar cheese
2 eggs, lightly beaten
1/2 teaspoon salt
1/2 teaspoon pepper
- Extras
Your favorite sauce for the ravioli (i.e. marinara/ marijuana)
Parmesan cheese
Basil
Fried vegetables
Shrimp
Fish slices
Chicken pieces
Make the Ravioli filling.
- In a small mixing bowl, add the ricotta and mash with a fork.
- Add in the 3-cheese blend, Cheddar cheese, eggs, salt, and pepper.
- Mix all ingredients thoroughly until you have a smooth, paste-like consistency.
- Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and place it in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
Make the Ravioli dough.
- Crack eggs into a large mixing bowl and beat them with a fork. Add water, oil, and salt. Mix.
- Add 1 cup flour to the bowl. Use a fork to mix the flour with the eggs, water, oil, and salt. Repeat with the rest of the flour. Mix until a smooth dough is formed.
- Clear and clean off a large work surface and dust it with flour. This is where you are going to roll out your dough.
- Take the dough out of the mixing bowl, shape it into a ball, and place it on your work surface. Knead for at least 10 minutes or until it becomes elastic.
- Dust a rolling pin with flour to prevent the dough from sticking. Roll out the dough until it is about 1/8 inch (1/3 cm) thick, or about the thickness of 2 stacked quarters.
- With a cookie cutter or upside-down water glass, cut out circles in the dough (will make about 15-20 dough circles).
- Ball up the unused dough and either roll it out and make a couple more raviolis, or wrap it and put in the freezer for another time. Dough can keep for weeks when frozen. Just make sure to wrap well so that it doesn’t suffer from freezer burn or absorb freezer odor.
Fill the Ravioli shells.
- Take the ravioli filling out of the refrigerator and place a tablespoon of it in middle of a dough.
- Fill a small bowl with water, dip your fingers in, and moisten around the outer edge of the dough circle.
- Fold the dough in half over the filling, making a half-moon shape. Be sure all the filling stays inside. Pinch the edges together and then seal the edges of the ravioli with a fork. Make sure to press firmly and go all the way around. This will add a “homemade” touch as well.
- Repeat this process for all your dough circles.
- Dust the finished ravioli with flour to keep them from sticking together.
Form the Shells and Fill Using a Ravioli maker.
- Roll the dough into two sheets
- Place one sheet on the ravioli maker, and form the filling cups.
- Fill with the ravioli mixture.
- Lay the second sheet of dough on top, and roll it out. This will seal in the filling.
- Remove and separate the finished raviolis.
Cook the Ravioli.
- Fill a large pot with water and bring to a boil.
- Place the ravioli in boiling water for 5-6 minutes, or until they float. You can also test for doneness by nibbling on the edges to test.
- If you don't want to make all the ravioli at one time, you can freeze the rest
- Take ravioli out of boiling water with large slotted spoon and place on warmed plates
Serve it up.
Top with your favorite sauce, grate some fresh cheese over it, and enjoy!
